summary: The authentication module introduces critical security vulnerabilities including SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, and unhandled null and error paths.

findings.title: SQL injection in findUser via string concatenation
findings.body: findUser concatenates the username argument directly into the SQL query string at src/auth.js:7-9 without escaping or parameterization, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL commands and bypass authentication.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g., db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username])).

findings.title: Unhandled null user leads to TypeError in login
findings.body: login attempts to read user.password without checking if findUser returned a valid user record at src/auth.js:14-15. If the user does not exist (e.g., null or undefined), this throws an unhandled TypeError.
findings.recommendation: Check if user exists before accessing properties (e.g., if (!user || user.password !== password) return null;).

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT secret
findings.body: JWT_SECRET is hardcoded in source code at src/auth.js:4. Committing secrets to source control compromises signing key security and prevents secret rotation across environments.
findings.recommendation: Retrieve the JWT secret from an environment variable (e.g., process.env.JWT_SECRET) or a secret manager.

findings.title: Uncaught exception on invalid JSON in parseSession
findings.body: parseSession calls JSON.parse(raw) without error handling at src/auth.js:21-24. Passing malformed JSON or null/undefined will throw an uncaught SyntaxError.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try/catch block and handle invalid input by returning null or an explicit error.

samples.summary: Found critical SQL injection vulnerability, missing module dependency, hardcoded secret, null reference crash, and unhandled JSON parse exceptions in auth.js.

findings.title: SQL Injection in findUser
findings.body: User input `username` is concatenated directly into the SQL query string in `findUser` at `src/auth.js:7-9`, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary SQL queries and bypass authentication.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries with placeholder bindings (e.g., `db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username])`) instead of string concatenation.

findings.title: Missing local database module dependency
findings.body: `src/auth.js:2` requires `./db`, but no `db.js` file or database module exists in the repository, which will cause a runtime `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` error upon loading.
findings.recommendation: Implement or provide the `./db` module and define the `query` method interface.

findings.title: Unhandled null user reference and plaintext password comparison in login
findings.body: In `login` at `src/auth.js:14-17`, `user.password` is accessed without checking if `user` exists, throwing a TypeError if the user is not found. In addition, passwords are compared directly in plaintext using loose equality rather than secure constant-time hashing.
findings.recommendation: Verify that `user` is non-null before checking credentials, and compare password hashes using a secure hashing library such as `bcrypt.compare`.

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT secret key in source code
findings.body: A static secret key `hardcoded-super-secret-key` is defined directly in `src/auth.js:4`, exposing signing keys in version control and preventing key rotation across environments.
findings.recommendation: Retrieve the JWT secret from environment variables (e.g. `process.env.JWT_SECRET`) and ensure the application fails fast if it is unset.

findings.title: Uncaught JSON.parse exception in parseSession
findings.body: `parseSession` at `src/auth.js:21-24` calls `JSON.parse(raw)` without a try/catch block and accesses `session.userId` without verifying that `session` is an object, leading to uncaught SyntaxError or TypeError crashes on invalid input.
findings.recommendation: Wrap `JSON.parse` in a try/catch block, handle parsing failures gracefully, and validate that `session` is a valid object before reading properties.

samples.summary: The authentication module contains critical security vulnerabilities including SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, unsafe user lookup, and unhandled parsing exceptions.

findings.title: SQL injection in findUser
findings.body: The findUser function concatenates the unescaped username parameter directly into the SQL query string in src/auth.js. An attacker can supply malicious SQL payloads to bypass authentication or extract sensitive database contents.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries, such as db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username]).

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT secret key
findings.body: The JWT signing key is hardcoded as a static string constant. If the repository is exposed or shared, attackers can forge valid authentication tokens for any user ID.
findings.recommendation: Retrieve the JWT secret from environment variables or a secrets manager via process.env.JWT_SECRET.

findings.title: Missing null check on user lookup and plaintext password comparison
findings.body: In login, if findUser returns null or undefined when no user matches, accessing user.password throws an unhandled TypeError. Additionally, passwords are compared in plaintext using loose equality (==) rather than secure hashed comparison.
findings.recommendation: Check that user exists before inspecting properties (e.g. if (!user) return null;) and use a secure hashing algorithm (such as bcrypt.compare) to verify passwords.

findings.title: Unhandled exception in parseSession
findings.body: parseSession calls JSON.parse on raw input without a try/catch block. Malformed JSON strings will throw an uncaught SyntaxError, and parsing 'null' will throw a TypeError when accessing session.userId.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try/catch block, handle invalid inputs gracefully, and verify session is an object before accessing userId.
